cases.note: a scalar condition is strict equality
a number condition matches the number
0 is a value, not the absent value
sibling keys must all hold
a bare list matches any of its values
an empty list matches nothing
a list of ids fetches a known set; an id no record has is no row
not excludes a value and never matches a record with no value
not with a list excludes every value in it
contains ignores case
an empty needle matches every value but never the absent value
startsWith matches a prefix
startsWith compares case-sensitively
endsWith matches a suffix, case-sensitively
several bounds on one field are one range
gt is strict
lte includes the bound
a range never matches a record with no value
text bounds compare text by code unit, so ISO dates order in time
a text bound against a number field never matches
exists false matches a field never written
exists true matches a field holding a value
the way to include the absent value is OR with exists false
a condition is read by its first operator: a range bound before not
OR holds when one branch does
AND holds when every branch does
NOT negates its clause, so it matches a record with no value
an empty AND always holds
an empty OR never holds
some holds when a member matches
some with an empty clause is 'has at least one'
none holds when no member matches
none with an empty clause is 'has none at all'
a quantifier reads a to-one relation as a list of at most one
quantifiers nest
a field cleared with '' is matched by no equality, '' included
cases.pending: clearing rule: whether '' and null are values or the absent value (WE reads both as absent)

cases.note: not never matches a field cleared with ''
cases.pending: clearing rule: whether '' and null are values or the absent value (WE reads both as absent)

cases.note: a field cleared with '' has no value
cases.pending: clearing rule: whether '' and null are values or the absent value (WE reads both as absent)

cases.note: a list held in one field is one value: equality with a member does not match it
cases.pending: multi-valued scalars: whether a property may hold several values, and what a comparison means against one that does (WE holds one value, a list being one json value)

cases.note: a single key orders the whole result, with or without a limit
text orders by code unit: capitals before small letters
a record with no value for the key comes last ascending
a record with no value for the key comes last descending too
a dotted key orders by a field of a related record, with a limit
several keys apply in the order written
limit keeps the first rows of the order
offset skips rows before the limit
a limit larger than the result keeps every row
an offset without a limit is refused
an included to-one relation is the record
an included to-one relation with no record is no value
an included to-many relation is the list of records
an included to-many relation with no members is an empty list
an included relation takes where and order
an included relation takes a limit after its order
an included relation takes select
includes nest
a reverse relation includes the record pointing at this one
an untyped relation reads each member as its own entity, in stored order
below an untyped relation a typed one nests; a member without it has none
a projection with limit 1 is the first matching record or no value, and takes an order
a projection without limit 1 is the list of matching records
a projection takes select
select names the fields a row carries; a field left out reads as no value
select carries relations as their members' ids
a list of entities answers with one list, each row naming its entity
order and limit apply to the whole list
an empty list of entities is an answer with no rows
an offset over several entities is refused
a record is listed once, under the first entity in the list that answers with it
cases.pending: union de-duplication: which entity a record two entities both answer with is listed under (WE lists it once, under the first entity in the list). The file's schemas give no record two entities, so this checks only that each record is listed once

cases.note: a falsy when is a query not asked: no rows, not loaded
a truthy when asks the query
a scope reads the records an anchor's relation holds, not the anchor
a list of anchors asks the same question of each
an empty list of anchors is still anchored, and answers with nothing
transitive reaches every record at any depth
levels walks depth by depth and stops after the last
levels keeps at most that many per record at each depth, order deciding
without an order a bounded walk keeps that many, whichever they are
limitPerAnchor keeps at most that many per anchor, order deciding
direction in reads the records whose relation holds the anchor
direction in takes a list of anchors
where narrows a walked result
a walked result is flat; including the inverse relation says where each row sits
a scope that does not name the anchors' entity reads the relation of that name which holds this entity
a scope along an untyped relation reads only the query's entity
a count projection is how many records the relation holds
a count takes a where
a transitive count counts at any depth along the relation
below an untyped relation each member counts for its own entity; one without the relation carries none
order may name a count projection, with a limit
without a limit a host may ignore an order by a projection; the rows are the same
a count rides on each included record
opens on the first result, flagged initial; a record created to match joins it
a record edited so it no longer matches leaves the result
a deleted record leaves the result
an edit to an included record is pushed
a count follows a member added to the relation
a walked result follows a record added under the anchor
subscribe false reads once: the answer stays what it was
author is a condition like any field: the agent that wrote the record
not on author leaves out an agent's records
